simple.meaning: גֵּז (gêz) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a fleece (as shorn); also mown grass.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Deuteronomy 18:4. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גֵּז (H1488) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a fleece (as shorn); also mown grass
definitions.full: H1488. gez גֵּז noun [masculine] shearing, mowing (Assyrian gizzu Zehnpf BAS i. 530 , Aramaic גִּיזָּא fleece ) — גֵּז Psa 72:6 , also construct Deut 18:4 ; Job 31:20 ; plural construct גִּזֵּי Amos 7:1 ; — shearing = thing sheared off, wool, fleece ׳ג צאֹן Deut 18:4 , ׳ג כְּבָשַׂי Job 31:20 ; mowing Amos 7:1 ( ׳ג הַמֶּלֶךְ compare RS Semitic i. 228 ); = land to be mown Psa 72:6 (but shearing in both, according to Hoffm ZAW 1883, 116 ff. SS).

occurrences.englishText: You shall give him the first fruits of your grain, of your new wine, and of your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep.
if his heart hasn’t blessed me,
He will come down like rain on the mown grass,
Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and behold, he formed locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and behold, it was the latter growth after the king’s harvest.
